title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a commutative ring and S = k{T} is the divided-power polynomial algebra, with T^{(i)}T^{(j)} = c_{ij} T^{(i+j)} and c_{ij} = binom(i+j, i). S^{+(N)} = ⊕_{i≥N} k·T^{(i)} is the N-th divided-power ideal. It is a free k-module with basis T^{(i)}, i≥N.

For a k-module M, the graded S-module is ω_N(M) = M⊗_k S^{+(N)} = ⊕_{i≥N} M·T^{(i)}, with each graded piece canonically isomorphic to M.

Corollary 1 (stated on this page, proof finished on the next page) has two parts.
(a) ω_N is a fully faithful functor from k-modules to graded S-modules (with degree-0 maps).
(b) The map φ: M → ∏_{i≥N} ω_N(M)_i, x ↦ (x·T^{(i)}), is a bijection onto the set of families (x_i) satisfying T^{(j)}x_i = c_{ij}x_{i+j} for all i≥N, j≥1.

Proof of (b):
- φ(x) satisfies the relations by the multiplication rule.
- φ is injective because x·T^{(N)} = 0 forces x = 0 (freeness).
- For surjectivity, write x_i = ξ_i T^{(i)}. The relation becomes binom(i+j,i)(ξ_{i+j} − ξ_i) = 0 for i≥N, j≥1. This is exactly the hypothesis of Theorem 1 (previous page): in an abelian group E, if binom(j,i)(x_j − x_i) = 0 for all j>i≥N, then the x_i are constant for i≥N. That theorem is proved by localizing at each p and using a lemma on the indices N + p^ε, with induction via N' = (N+1)/p − 1.

Proof of (a): a degree-0 S-linear map ω_N(M) → ω_N(M') is a family of k-maps u_i: M → M' compatible with multiplication by T^{(j)}. That compatibility means c_{ij}(u_{i+j} − u_i) = 0. Theorem 1, applied in E = Hom_k(M, M'), forces all u_i to be equal. Hence Hom_k(M, M') ≅ Hom_gr(ω_N M, ω_N M').

The next page reformulates this: ω_N has a right adjoint π_N, given by compatible families. Part (b) says the unit M → π_N ω_N M is an isomorphism, which is equivalent to full faithfulness. ω_N(M) is then the truncation τ_{≥N} of ω_0(M) = M⊗k{T}.

The purpose is evidently foundational for the divided-power de Rham complex lectures. One can recover M from any divided-power truncation of M⊗k{T}, uniformly over any base ring including ℤ, where denominators are unavailable. This needs a genuinely arithmetic lemma about binomial coefficients.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The argument is correct given Theorem 1. Freeness of S^{+(N)} over k makes ξ_i well defined, and Theorem 1 is applied with c_{ij} = binom(i+j,i), matching its indexing with j' = i+j.
Slip: the product in (b) is first written ∏_{i≥0} ω_N(M)_i and then ∏_{i≥N}. Harmless, since ω_N(M)_i = 0 for i<N.
Slip: 'A-modules' should be 'k-modules' (crossed out in the manuscript). In (a), Hom must mean degree-preserving S-linear maps; this is implicit.
On the previous page ω_N(M) is written M⊗_S S^{+(N)}; it should be M⊗_k S^{+(N)}.

ideas.what: The divided-power polynomial algebra k{T}, its divided-power ideals S^{+(N)}, and the multiplication rule T^{(i)}T^{(j)} = binom(i+j,i)T^{(i+j)}
ideas.modern_name: divided power algebra Γ_k(T) and its PD-filtration

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of M ↦ M⊗_k Γ^{≥N}(T) into graded Γ(T)-modules; M recovered as compatible families via the right adjoint π_N
ideas.modern_name: full faithfulness of truncated divided-power base change; adjunction unit isomorphism

ideas.what: Use of Theorem 1 (binomial annihilators force constancy) to make the statement hold over arbitrary k, including ℤ
ideas.modern_name: gcd/Kummer–Lucas type arguments on binomial coefficients

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but routine corollary: a divided-power truncation of M⊗k{T} remembers M and its morphisms integrally. It is a foundational lemma for the 1976 PD de Rham lectures. No new connection or unexploited result is visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'satisfaisant aux φ condition' is likely 'satisfaisant aux conditions'; the 'φ' is a misread.
'des A-modules' has A crossed out; read 'k-modules'.
In (a), 'Soient M, M' des k..' means 'des k-modules'; 'Hom(ω_N(M), ω_N(M'))' has a crossed-out symbol before ω_N.
The marginal number '23' at the bottom is the page number.
